reader.decision: Reject lowering the CDN TTL. Approve event-driven eviction: every pod subscribes to `price.changed` and pops the SKU. Also lower the per-pod cache TTL to 300 as a backstop. Confirm where startup subscription goes, since `shop/app.py` was not found.
reader.decision_reason: The message says the price API is never cached by the CDN (`/api/*` has `cache: false`), so the CDN TTL change cannot help. The stale prices come from per-pod caches, and only one of six pods is cleared on admin change. The event-driven fix removes that cause using the existing Redis channel.

reconstruction.problem: After an admin price change, customers see the old price for up to an hour. Each of six `shop-api` pods keeps its own in-process `price_cache` with TTL 3600. `update_price` in `admin/prices.py` evicts the SKU only on the pod that handled the POST. It then publishes `price.changed`, but only `search/indexer.py` subscribes, so the other five pods keep the old price.
reconstruction.what_breaks: Reloads show a mix of 34.90 and 39.90 depending on which pod answers. Checkout reads `/api/prices` too, so customers pay the old price. Stale entries last up to 3600 seconds. The CDN is not involved: `/api/*` is `cache: false`, and the 3600 TTL in `cdn/rules.yaml` applies to `/product/*` pages that hold no price.
reconstruction.fix: Add `on_price_changed(event)` in `pricing/service.py` that calls `price_cache.pop(event["sku"], None)`. Subscribe to `price.changed` on every pod at startup, probably in `shop/app.py`, though that file was not found. Keep the local pop in `admin/prices.py`. Lower the per-pod cache TTL from 3600 to 300 as a backstop. Make no change to `cdn/rules.yaml`. Alternative: set the per-pod TTL to 60 and add no subscriber.
reconstruction.cost: The recommended fix costs one subscriber thread per pod. A pod that misses a pub/sub message stays stale until the 300-second TTL expires. The alternative needs no Redis dependency in the pods, but staleness is bounded at 60 seconds, not removed, and the database gets more reads.

follow_up_questions: Where does `shop-api` start up and register subscribers, given `shop/app.py` was not found?
Is a stale price for up to 60 seconds acceptable to the business? This only matters if you prefer the TTL-only alternative.
reader.closing_answer: Subscribe every pod to `price.changed` and evict the SKU, with the per-pod TTL lowered to 300 as a backstop. I don't choose the 60-second TTL-only option unless the business confirms a minute of staleness is fine and wants no new moving part.
